**Project 2** - Released Tuesday April 21st, Due Wednesday May 13th at noon ::: # Today: Control Flow ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ### Control Flow * The flow of execution of `R` code. * So far, our primary rule: Place your code in the order that you want `R` to evaluate it. ::: {.fragment} Incorrect order: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} crash_data <- read_csv("data/pdx_crash_2018_page1.csv") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-error} ``` Error in `read_csv()`: ! could not find function "read_csv" ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} library(tidyverse) ``` ::: :::
::: {.fragment} Correct order: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} library(tidyverse) crash_data <- read_csv("data/pdx_crash_2018_page1.csv") ``` ::: ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ### Control Flow * Can also get `R` to conditionally run code blocks or run code blocks multiple times. * Control structures allow you to control the flow of execution. * Main tools we will use to control the flow: + `if()` and `else()` + `stop()` and `stopifnot()` + `for()` loops :::: {.columns .fragment} ::: {.column width='50%'} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} die_roll <- sample(1:6, size = 1) if(die_roll == 6) { print("Biggest number!") } else { print(die_roll) } ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 3 ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width='50%'} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} for(i in 1:6){ print(i * 10) } ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 10 [1] 20 [1] 30 [1] 40 [1] 50 [1] 60 ``` ::: ::: ::: :::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ### Come Back to Logical Operators * To control the flow, we need to be really comfortable with logical operators. :::: {.columns} ::: {.column .fragment width='50%'} Or operators: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} a <- c(TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE) b <- c(TRUE, FALSE) a | b ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] TRUE FALSE TRUE TRUE ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} a || b ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-error} ``` Error in `a || b`: ! 'length = 4' in coercion to 'logical(1)' ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} xor(a, b) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] FALSE FALSE TRUE TRUE ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width='50%'} * Which is vectorized? * What is recycling again? * What is going on with `||`? ::: :::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ### Logical Operators And operators: :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width='50%'} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} a <- c(TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE) b <- c(TRUE, FALSE) a & b ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] TRUE FALSE FALSE FALSE ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} a && b ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-error} ``` Error in `a && b`: ! 'length = 4' in coercion to 'logical(1)' ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width='50%' .nonincremental} * Which is vectorized? * What is recycling again? * What is going on with `&&`? ::: :::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ### Element-wise comparison (`&` and `|`) vs. single-element comparison (`&&` and `||`) :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width='50%' .fragment} **Element-wise comparison**: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} a <- c(TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE) b <- c(TRUE, FALSE) a & b ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] TRUE FALSE FALSE FALSE ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} a | b ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] TRUE FALSE TRUE TRUE ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width='50%'} ::: {.fragment} **Single-element comparison**: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} a && b ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-error} ``` Error in `a && b`: ! 'length = 4' in coercion to 'logical(1)' ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} a || b ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-error} ``` Error in `a || b`: ! 'length = 4' in coercion to 'logical(1)' ``` ::: ::: :::
::: {.fragment} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} a <- TRUE b <- FALSE a && b ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] FALSE ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} a || b ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] TRUE ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: :::: - More exploration of `&&` and `||` in our activity today - For further discussion of the differences, see [here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/6558921/difference-between-boolean-operators-and-and-between-and-in-r) ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ### Logical Operators Not operator: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} a <- c(TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE) b <- c(TRUE, FALSE) !a ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] FALSE TRUE TRUE FALSE ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} !a & b ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] FALSE FALSE TRUE FALSE ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} !(a & b) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] FALSE TRUE TRUE TRUE ``` ::: ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ### Comparison Operators :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width='50%'} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} x <- c(1, 3, 5) y <- c(1, 4, 2) z <- c(3, 2) x < y x <= y x > y x >= y ``` ::: ::: ::: {.column width='50%' .fragment} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} x == y x != y x != z z %in% x x %in% z ``` ::: ::: :::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ### Comparison Operators :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width='50%'} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} x <- c(1, 3, 5) y <- c(1, 4, 2) z <- c(3, 2) x < y ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] FALSE TRUE FALSE ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} x <= y ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] TRUE TRUE FALSE ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} x > y ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] FALSE FALSE TRUE ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} x >= y ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] TRUE FALSE TRUE ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width='50%' .fragment} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} x == y ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] TRUE FALSE FALSE ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} x != y ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] FALSE TRUE TRUE ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} x != z ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] TRUE TRUE TRUE ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} z %in% x ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] TRUE FALSE ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} x %in% z ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] FALSE TRUE FALSE ``` ::: ::: ::: :::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ### Sidebar: Operators as functions - Operators are just functions with funky notation - Typically, we use operators with **infix** notation: ::: {.fragment} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} x == y ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] TRUE FALSE FALSE ``` ::: ::: ::: - However, we can use **prefix** notation just like other functions we are used to: ::: {.fragment} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} `==`(x, y) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] TRUE FALSE FALSE ``` ::: ::: ::: - Note the use of backticks. - This works for all operators! ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ### Conditional Control Flow `R` will conditionally execute code via `if` statements. The basic one-line form is: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} if (condition) true_action if (condition) true_action else false_action ``` ::: The basic multi-line form is: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} if (condition) { true_action } if (condition) { true_action } else { false_action } ``` ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ### Conditional Control Flow `R` will conditionally execute code via `if` statements. ::: {.fragment} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} x <- c(1, 3, 5) if (3 %in% x){ print("Vector contains 3.") } ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "Vector contains 3." ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} if (4 %in% x){ print("Vector contains 4.") } ``` ::: :::
::: {.fragment} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} if (4 %in% x){ print("Vector contains 4.") } else { print("Vector does not contain 4.") } ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "Vector does not contain 4." ``` ::: ::: ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ### Conditional Control Flow `if()` is not vectorized! ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} x <- c(1, 3, 5) if (x == 1){ print("Vector contains 1.") } ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-error} ``` Error in `if (x == 1) ...`: ! the condition has length > 1 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} if (x == 3){ print("Vector contains 3.") } ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-error} ``` Error in `if (x == 3) ...`: ! the condition has length > 1 ``` ::: ::: - Alternative condition? ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ### Conditional Control Flow `if()` is not vectorized! Alternative condition? ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} if (x %in% 3){ print("Vector contains 3.") } ``` ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ### Conditional Control Flow `if()` is not vectorized! Alternative condition? ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} if (x %in% 3){ print("Vector contains 3.") } ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-error} ``` Error in `if (x %in% 3) ...`: ! the condition has length > 1 ``` ::: ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ### Conditional Control Flow `if()` is not vectorized! Alternative condition? ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} if (x %in% 3){ print("Vector contains 3.") } ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-error} ``` Error in `if (x %in% 3) ...`: ! the condition has length > 1 ``` ::: :::
::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} if (3 %in% x){ print("Vector contains 3.") } ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "Vector contains 3." ``` ::: ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ### Collapsing Logical Vectors Because `if` is not vectorized, it is often helpful to collapse logical vectors to a single value. - Enter: `any()` and `all()`
:::: {.columns} ::: {.column width='50%' .fragment} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} x <- c(1, 3, 5) any(x == 1) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] TRUE ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} if (any(x == 1)){ print("Vector contains 1.") } ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "Vector contains 1." ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} if (any(x == 3)){ print("Vector contains 3.") } ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "Vector contains 3." ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width='50%' .fragment} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} all(x <= 4) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] FALSE ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} all(x <= 5) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] TRUE ``` ::: ::: ::: :::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ### Continuing the Conditional Executions :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width='50%' .fragment} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} x = 3 if (x < 0) { print("x is negative") } else if (x > 0) { print("x is positive") } else { print("x is zero") } ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "x is positive" ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width='50%' .fragment} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} x = 0 if (x < 0) { print("x is negative") } else if (x > 0) { print("x is positive") } else { print("x is zero") } ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "x is zero" ``` ::: ::: ::: :::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ### Saving Results :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width='50%'} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} height_in <- 82 if (height_in >= 84) { "Center" } else if (height_in >= 78) { "Forward" } else if (height_in >= 75) { "Shooting Guard" } else { "Point Guard" } ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "Forward" ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width='50%'} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} if (height_in >= 84) { position <- "Center" } else if (height_in >= 78) { position <- "Forward" } else if (height_in >= 75) { position <- "Shooting Guard" } else { position <- "Point Guard" } position ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "Forward" ``` ::: ::: ::: :::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ### Vectorized `if() else()` :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width='50%' .fragment .nonincremental} * `ifelse()` runs operations on an entire vector. ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} height_in <- c(82, 74, 87) position <- ifelse(height_in >= 84, "Center", "not Center") position ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "not Center" "not Center" "Center" ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width='50%' .fragment .nonincremental} * `case_when()` provides a more flexible alternative. ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} position <- case_when( height_in >= 84 ~ "Center", height_in >= 78 ~ "Forward", height_in >= 75 ~ "Shooting Guard", TRUE ~ "Point Guard" ) position ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "Forward" "Point Guard" "Center" ``` ::: ::: ::: :::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ### Error Checking * Often want to validate user inputs or function assumptions. + Will see this in action next time when discussing functions. * If an input is incorrect or an assumption isn't met, then want to report the error and **stop the code**. ::: {.fragment} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} height_in <- c(82, 74, 87) stopifnot(is.character(height_in)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-error} ``` Error: ! is.character(height_in) is not TRUE ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} stopifnot(is.numeric(height_in)) ``` ::: ::: * Want a more helpful error message! ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ### Error Checking Alternative for more informative error messages: * Check inputs with `if()` * And then `stop()` if they are wrong. ::: {.fragment} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} height_in <- c(82, 74, 87) if(!is.character(height_in)) { stop('This function only works for character inputs.\n', 'You have provided an object of class: ', class(x)) } ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-error} ``` Error: ! This function only works for character inputs. You have provided an object of class: numeric ``` ::: ::: ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ### Control Flow Recap * The flow of execution of `R` code. * Order still matters. * But now we can: + Run subsets of the code with `if()` and `else()`. + Check for errors with `stop()`. * Very helpful for building functions (Wednesday) * Will add in `for()` loops and other iteration methods next week. * Also need to weave in best practices. + Lots of ways to do something. Which is best? # Activity Time

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
